wstep: This card describes the NCHFP recipe for apple butter: apples cooked in apple cider and vinegar, pressed into a pulp, cooked with white and brown sugar and spices, and processed in a boiling-water bath. [T:SLO-087,SLO-224,SLO-225]

akapity: NCHFP uses 8 pounds (about 3.6 kg) of apples, 2 cups of apple cider, 2 cups of vinegar, 2 1/4 cups of white sugar, 2 1/4 cups of packed brown sugar, 2 tablespoons of ground cinnamon and 1 tablespoon of ground cloves; this makes about 9 to 10 pint jars. [T:SLO-224]
Despite the name, apple butter contains no butter: it is a thick, spiced apple pulp cooked with sugar. [T:SLO-224,SLO-225]
NCHFP suggests Jonathan, Winesap, Stayman, Golden Delicious, McIntosh or other tasty apple varieties. [T:SLO-224]
Use fresh apples, free from any signs of decay or mold. [T:SLO-048]
NCHFP uses US measures: a cup holds about 237 ml. [T:ACI-195]

The recipe does not give the strength of the vinegar; JarAtlas rule (cautious): use white distilled or cider vinegar labelled 5% or 6% acidity, and do not dilute 10% vinegar with water to make 5%. [T:SLO-224,ACI-211]
Sterilize the half-pint and pint jars; NCHFP says quart jars need not be presterilized. [T:SLO-226]

NCHFP puts the empty jars right side up on the rack in a boiling-water canner and fills the canner and jars with hot (not boiling) water to 1 inch (about 2.5 cm) above the tops of the jars. [T:SLO-120]
To sterilize empty jars, NCHFP boils them for 10 minutes below 1000 ft, and above that 1 minute longer for each additional thousand feet. [T:SLO-118]
JarAtlas rule for metres: boil the jars for 10 minutes up to 300 m, and add 1 minute for every further 300 m or part of it. [T:SLO-119]
Wash the apples, remove the stems, cut them into quarters and remove the cores. [T:SLO-225]
Cook them slowly in the apple cider and vinegar until soft. [T:SLO-225]
Press the fruit through a colander, food mill or strainer. [T:SLO-225]
Cook the pulp with the sugar and spices, stirring frequently. [T:SLO-225]
To test for doneness, take a spoonful and hold it away from the steam for 2 minutes: the butter is done if it stays mounded on the spoon. [T:SLO-225]
Another test: spoon a little onto a plate; when no rim of liquid separates around the edge, the butter is ready for canning. [T:SLO-225]
Just before filling, remove and drain the hot sterilized jars one at a time. [T:SLO-120]
Fill the hot apple butter into the jars, leaving 1/4 inch (about 0.6 cm) of headspace. [T:SLO-226]
Put on the lids and process in a boiling-water canner. [T:SLO-226]
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m) process half-pint and pint jars for 5 minutes and quart jars for 10 minutes. [T:SLO-226,ACI-176]
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased. [T:ACI-015]
At 1001–6000 ft (above 300 m up to 1800 m) process half-pints and pints for 10 minutes and quarts for 15 minutes. [T:SLO-226,ACI-176]
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m) process half-pints and pints for 15 minutes and quarts for 20 minutes. [T:SLO-226,ACI-176]
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m. [T:ACI-176]
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage. [T:ACI-015]
NCHFP times are for US jar sizes: a pint holds about 473 ml and a quart about 946 ml. [T:ACI-174]
JarAtlas rule (NCHFP does not test metric jars): for a jar of up to 473 ml use the pint time, and for a larger jar of up to 946 ml, for example 0.5 l or 0.9 l, use the quart time. [T:ACI-175]
This NCHFP recipe gives no time for jars larger than a quart, such as 1 l, so JarAtlas recommends smaller jars. [T:ACI-175]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): a jar of up to 473 ml gets the shorter pint time, so sterilize it like a pint jar. [T:SLO-226,ACI-175]
When you take the hot jars out of the canner, do not retighten the lids or bands; this can cut through the gasket and cause seal failures. [T:SLO-210]

Cool the jars at room temperature for 12 to 24 hours, then remove only the screw bands (the metal rings of two-piece lids), leaving the flat lids on the jars, and test the seal: press the middle of the lid, and if it springs up when you release it, the jar is not sealed. [T:SLO-196,SLO-212]

NCHFP calls Mason-type canning jars with self-sealing two-piece lids (a flat lid and a screw band) the best choice, and this seal test and the method on this card assume them; NCHFP does not recommend other commercial jars whose mouths cannot be sealed with two-piece canning lids for canning any food at home. [T:SLO-223,SLO-212]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): use this card only with jars that take two-piece canning lids; it gives no method for twist-off jars or jars with glass lids, so do not use them for this recipe. [T:SLO-223]
A sealed lid is concave, curved down slightly in the centre; if the centre is flat or bulging, the jar may not be sealed. [T:SLO-196]
If a jar has not sealed at this check, keep it in the refrigerator and eat it within several days. [T:SLO-197]

Store sealed jars in a clean, cool, dark, dry place, not above 95 °F (35 °C) and not near hot pipes, a stove or a furnace, in an uninsulated attic or in direct sunlight; in such conditions the food may spoil. [T:SLO-198]

JarAtlas rule (cautious): keep an opened jar in the refrigerator; NCHFP says this for its reduced-sugar apple butter and for opened jams and jellies, but gives no storage time for this apple butter after opening. [T:SLO-227]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): keep an opened jar in the refrigerator and use it within 1 week. [T:SLO-322]
Before using a stored jar, check that the lid is tight and holds a vacuum: a good seal has a concave centre. [T:SLO-191]
Look for streaks of dried food running from the top of the jar, rising air bubbles and unnatural colour. [T:SLO-191]
When opening the jar, check for an unnatural smell, spurting liquid and cotton-like mould on the food or under the lid. [T:SLO-191]
Do not taste food from a jar with an unsealed lid or with signs of spoilage. [T:SLO-190]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): throw out such a jar. [T:SLO-190]
If you see mold or other signs of spoilage in an opened jar, throw out its whole contents. [T:SLO-013]
